samples.summary: Cell path now falls through to `[0,0]` in cases the old code handled, so Home/End can collapse the caret to offset 0
samples.evidence: The rewritten guard is `if (layoutCell && !layoutCell.merged && cell && cbi >= 0)`. The old code entered its body on `layoutCell && !layoutCell.merged` alone and, on any inner failure, still returned `[0, getBlockTextLength(doc.getBlock(pos.blockId))]` — i.e. the whole block. Two new failure conditions (`cell` missing, `cbi < 0`) now skip the block entirely and drop to `const lb = layout.blocks.find((b) => b.block.id === pos.blockId); if (!lb) return [0, 0];` (4101-4102). A cell-inner block is never a member of `layout.blocks`, so the result is `[0, 0]`. `cbi < 0` is exactly the "block created since the last layout" case the new comment cites (Enter/paste splitting a cell block, or a remote edit), because `cbi` is now computed against the *layout snapshot's* `resolved.dataBlock` instead of the live document. `getVisualLineEnd` then returns `{offset: 0}` and `getVisualLineStart` likewise, so End/Home move the caret to the start of the block rather than leaving it where it is. `getWrapAffinity` is unaffected (start 0 ⇒ 'backward'), which is why the new tests do not surface it.

samples.summary: Block-length fallback switched from the live document block to the layout snapshot's block, so it can report a pre-edit length
samples.evidence: `return [0, getBlockTextLength(cell.blocks[cbi])];` replaces the old `getBlockTextLength(this.doc.getBlock(pos.blockId))`. `cell` comes from `resolved.dataBlock`, i.e. the block reference held by the cached `LayoutBlock`; the layout is only recomputed inside `render()` (editor.ts:1918, via rAF), while `getWrapAffinity` is invoked synchronously *before* `requestRender()` (e.g. text-editor.ts:559-561, 585-588, 637-647). With a store whose `getDocument()` returns fresh objects (Yorkie-backed), that reference is the pre-edit block and the returned range end is the pre-edit length. This fallback is reached precisely when `pos.offset` runs past the laid-out lines — i.e. right after an insertion — so `getVisualLineEnd` on that path would stop short of the real block end.

samples.summary: Unbounded `while (true)` parent-chain walk is now on the per-keystroke path; a self-referential/cyclic `blockParentMap` entry hangs the editor
samples.evidence: `resolveNestedTableLayout` walks `while (true) { const parentInfo = layout.blockParentMap.get(topTableId); if (!parentInfo) break; topTableId = parentInfo.tableBlockId; }` with no visited-set and no depth cap. The delta makes `getWrapAffinity` (called on every insertion/composition step) reach this walk for every cell caret, widening the exposure of a map entry that points at itself or into a cycle from a occasional layout/selection query to every keystroke. The map is normally built from an acyclic layout walk, hence low confidence, but the new comment explicitly reasons about the map describing shapes the layout/document no longer has — the same staleness argument that motivates the other guards applies here and is not guarded.

samples.summary: Per-keystroke affinity resolution now runs a full nested-table resolution including `computeMergedCellLineLayouts` per nesting level
samples.evidence: `getWrapAffinity` → `getVisualLineRange` → `resolveNestedTableLayout` which, for each nesting segment, scans every line of the enclosing cell and calls `computeMergedCellLineLayouts(cell.lines, ...)` (table-layout.ts:396-418). This runs on every inserted character while the caret is in any cell, where the previous implementation was a single `layout.blocks.find`. Correctness is unaffected; noting the added per-keystroke cost.

finding.summary: getWrapAffinity now routes every keystroke through getVisualLineRange's unguarded `rows[rowIndex].cells[colIndex]` dereference (possible TypeError)
finding.evidence: getWrapAffinity (4140-4143) is called after every insertText/composition commit (lines 333, 559, 587, 647, 698, 744, 3646, 3701, 3773, 5242). It now enters the cell branch of getVisualLineRange, which does `const cell = tableBlock.tableData!.rows[cellInfo.rowIndex].cells[cellInfo.colIndex];` (4063) with no optional chaining, using indices from `blockParentMap` — a map that is only rebuilt inside recomputeLayout (editor.ts:1306-1313), i.e. on the next animation frame. If the doc's table shrank since the last layout (row/column delete queued via markDirty, layout not yet recomputed), `rows[rowIndex]` is undefined and the expression throws `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'cells')` inside the input handler. Before this change getWrapAffinity never touched table layout, so this dereference was only reachable from Home/End/vertical-move.

verdict.reason: The finding's central evidence — an unguarded `tableBlock.tableData!.rows[cellInfo.rowIndex].cells[cellInfo.colIndex]` in the cell branch of `getVisualLineRange` — is not present in the repository. text-editor.ts:4071-4076 reads `const resolved = resolveNestedTableLayout(...)`, `const layoutCell = resolved?.layoutTable.cells[cellInfo.rowIndex]?.[cellInfo.colIndex]`, and `const cell = resolved?.dataBlock.tableData?.rows[cellInfo.rowIndex]?.cells[cellInfo.colIndex]`, then gates all use behind `if (layoutCell && !layoutCell.merged && cell && cbi >= 0)`. A stale blockParentMap index (row/col no longer existing) therefore yields `undefined` and falls through to the block-wide path at 4101-4108 rather than throwing — precisely the degradation documented in the comment at 4063-4068. Remaining accesses inside the branch are guarded too (`blockBoundaries[cbi] ?? 0`, `layoutCell.lines[li]?.runs ?? []`, and `cell.blocks[cbi]` where cbi comes from a checked findIndex). The helper it delegates to, resolveNestedTableLayout, is likewise fully guarded (table-layout.ts:352 `if (!lb?.layoutTable) return undefined`, :383-384 `tl.cells[rowIndex]?.[colIndex]` with merged/undefined early return, :386 optional-chained cellData, :424 `if (!nextBlock?.tableData) return undefined`). The unguarded `tableData!.rows[i].cells[j]` pattern does exist at other, unrelated call sites (e.g. text-editor.ts:1997, 2538, 3921) but not on the getWrapAffinity path the finding describes.
